HPCC Fire Map Honored with International GIS Award

📅 2026-07-22 ✍️ Las Vegas Optic 🏷️ GIS, Esri User Conference, Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon Fire, fire mapping, NMFWRI, New Mexico, cartography, map design, award, environmental mapping
🔗 Read the source article →

💡 Quick summary

A GIS map depicting the devastating 2022 Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon Fire in New Mexico won first place in the Place Perception category at the Esri User Conference map gallery, earning international recognition for its powerful visual storytelling of wildfire progression and post-fire flooding.

📌 Key takeaways

  • Dana Heusinkveld, a GIS research specialist at NMFWRI based at Highlands University, designed the award-winning map depicting the 2022 Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon Fire
  • The fire burned more than 340,000 acres in northern New Mexico, destroyed hundreds of buildings, and was followed by damaging post-fire floods
  • The map won first place in Place Perception, one of a dozen categories at the Esri UC map gallery, which attracted over 600 entries from around the world
  • Esri judges praised the map's "powerful sense of progression through its skillful use of color and composition," with chart colors beautifully coordinated with the map
  • NMFWRI's GIS team also presented to over 100 colleagues on the HPCC Post-fire Resource Hub and ReSHAPE, a tool for collecting and analyzing fuel treatment and wildfire data nationally
